title: wkagent-name Python Prototype: 10x Speed Improvement
desc: Python reimplementation of wkagent-name.ps1 using ctypes Win32 API. Target <300ms vs 2900ms PowerShell. File: D:/GitHub/wkappbot-sdk/wkagent-name.py
steps: MOTIVATION: wkagent-name.cmd takes 2.9s because PowerShell runtime startup is ~1.5-2s. Python with ctypes calls Win32 directly with no runtime overhead. Target: <300ms (~10x faster).

KEY APIS USED: CreateToolhelp32Snapshot + Process32First/Next for parent chain map. NtQueryInformationProcess via PEB walk for cmdlines. OpenProcess + ReadProcessMemory for PEB traversal. These are the same APIs PowerShell CimInstance uses internally, minus the .NET + WMI overhead.

RESOLUTION ORDER (same as PS1): (1) env WKHARNESS_AGENT_MODEL. (2) Walk parent chain checking --model flag in each cmdline. (3) Read ~/.claude/wkharness/active-session-<slug>.json with ts field (NOT timestamp). (4) Return ROOT if nothing found.
KNOWN BUG FIXED: original Haiku prototype used c_char_p * 260 for szExeFile -- wrong (pointer not array). Correct: ctypes.c_char * 260. Also active-session field is ts not timestamp.
OPTIMIZATION TODO: get_process_name() calls CreateToolhelp32Snapshot per PID -- should reuse parent_chain map from get_parent_chain() call. One snapshot read covers all processes.
OUTPUT FORMAT (same as PS1): stdout = model name only. stderr = pid + truncated cmdline + elapsed ms.

KNOWN ISSUE: PEB offset for RTL_USER_PROCESS_PARAMETERS is 0x20 on x64 (pointer to RTL struct), CommandLine is at +0x70 within that struct. These offsets are Windows version-specific. WMIC fallback used when NtQueryInformationProcess fails.
TESTING: run python wkagent-name.py and compare output to wkagent-name.cmd -- both should output same model name.
